spots.s: Rocky mid-river island reached by a footbridge slung under the Lee Bridge — sunbathing rocks, quarry pond and skyline views that make an effortless first date.
Free, world-class collection (Fabergé eggs to Kehinde Wiley) with a sculpture garden and late hours — Richmond's most reliable rainy-day date.
100-acre Gilded Age estate with Japanese and Italian gardens, waterfalls and free wildlife exhibits — built for long walking conversations.
Two presidents, wild ironwork and bluffs high over the James — the river overlook here is one of the city's best (and oddly romantic) sunset walks.
“The view that named Richmond” — a Church Hill terrace above a bend in the James; bring takeout and watch the river turn gold at dusk.
1.25 miles of canal-side path, murals and history medallions linking Shockoe to the river — the easy pre-dinner date loop downtown.
Nine walkable blocks of indie shops, record stores and cafés — Richmond's best aimless-afternoon wander, capped with a Byrd movie.
1928 movie palace running cheap second-run films under a Czech crystal chandelier, with Saturday-night Wurlitzer organ preludes — best-value date in town.
50 acres with a glass-domed conservatory, rose garden and the winter GardenFest light walk — date-gold in every season.
Patrick Henry demanded liberty or death here in 1775 — tours and summer reenactments atop atmospheric Church Hill.
Moody shrine to Edgar Allan Poe in Richmond's oldest house, with an enchanted garden that hosts evening Unhappy Hours (Apr–Oct).
Giant-screen Dome theater and hands-on halls inside a grand 1919 train station — a playful, zero-pressure date option on Broad.
Jefferson designed it; free tours reveal the hidden interior dome — pair with Capitol Square's shaded lawns and skyline peeks.
An actual 500-year-old English manor shipped over brick by brick, with formal gardens above the James — nobody expects it.
Former industrial grid packed with a dozen-plus breweries, cideries and a meadery within stumbling distance — Väsen, The Veil and Ardent anchor the crawl.
Urban winery with a big lawn, bocce, firepits and live music in Scott's Addition — picnic-blanket date energy without leaving the city.
Guided class III–IV whitewater rafting through downtown — the only US city where rapids run past skyscrapers; tubing and kayak trips too.
Brand-new-for-2026 Diamond District ballpark — Squirrels baseball, fireworks nights and cheap seats make the easiest low-stakes date going.
Elevated floodwall path over the James with the postcard skyline view — hit it at golden hour, then drinks in Manchester.

nightlife.s: 1,500-cap former movie palace downtown — the room every mid-size hip-hop, R&B and rock tour plays; the GA floor actually dances.
Sweet-spot 800-cap room booking funk, hip-hop, jam and R&B most nights — grown-up crowd, good sightlines, easy parking.

nightlife.n: Richmond Music Hall at Capital Ale House
nightlife.s: Club shows in the hall under the downtown ale house — catch a band, then debate 50-plus taps upstairs; comfortable solo hang.
Beloved 200-cap incubator where RVA bands cut their teeth — cheap covers, eclectic calendar, talk-to-strangers energy.
Shockoe Bottom stalwart for metal, punk and touring rock — gritty in exactly the right way.
Historic firehouse turned gallery-venue — punk shows, art markets and the wildest First Friday openings; free-spirited crowd.
Newer Broad Street hall booking EDM, hip-hop and national club tours on a big-room sound system.
40-year Shockoe Slip institution — DJs run hip-hop, R&B and throwbacks Fri–Sat beneath the restaurant; dress code, grown crowd.
Southside restaurant-lounge where DJs spin hip-hop and R&B Thursday through Saturday — dressy, 30-plus crowd.
Home of Richmond's famous weekend drag brunch plus high-energy dance nights — camp, cocktails, zero pretension.
55,000 sq ft of duckpin bowling, karaoke rooms, comedy and DJs — goes full nightclub (21+) after 8:30 on weekends.
20th-floor perch above Main Street — the highest drink in Richmond, with river and skyline views built for date night.
Pink-hued art-hotel rooftop on Broad — golden-hour cocktails over the skyline, steps from the First Fridays galleries.
Carytown's nationally noticed cocktail den — “full pours, fair prices,” a deep rum list and bartenders worth the counter seat; ideal first-drink venue.
Password-at-the-bookshelf 1920s juice joint on East Main — theatrical, intimate and a guaranteed conversation starter.

eats.s: Downtown's intimate upstairs omakase lounge — a 13-course chef-curated tasting that finally gave Richmond a true sushi counter night.
30-seat Museum District institution voted Richmond's best sushi for two decades straight — counter seats and quiet confidence.
Fan institution since 1999 — sushi rolls, a bucket of tots and a dive-bar soul; open till 2a and never boring.
Scott's Addition sushi-and-poke spot with fish that punches above the fast-casual vibe — easy pre-brewery dinner.
Stylish Midlothian standby pairing fresh sushi with pan-Asian entrées and a proper bar — the west-end date-dinner default.
West End mainstay for impeccably fresh sashimi and hand rolls plus pan-Asian steaks — polished without being stuffy.
Henrico's authentic Japanese comfort-food stop — the signature spicy kara ramen and sake list are worth the Broad Street haul.
Build-your-own bowls near VCU with rich broths and fresh toppings — cheap, fast and satisfying before a show.
All-you-can-eat KBBQ on Midlothian Turnpike — grill-it-yourself banchan-loaded feasts that force conversation.
Short Pump's all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ and hot pot combo — tabletop grills, bubbling broths, group-dinner insurance.
Mochi, milk tea and an in-house bakery of airy mousse cakes and croissants by Willow Lawn — a low-key afternoon-date ace.
An Bui's 30-year Vietnamese anchor — legendary pho and one of America's great beer lists under one W Broad roof.
No-frills West Broad pho house locals call the city's best bowl — fast, cheap and restorative.
Longtime family-run Vietnamese off Broad — deep-broth pho and crispy spring rolls without a wait or a scene.

chinese.s: The James Beard-nominated Sichuan master's in-town flagship — scallion bubble pancake, dry-fried eggplant and proper 麻辣 heat in the Hofheimer Building.
The original Richmond-area Chang outpost since 2012 — bring a group, over-order, and let the cumin lamb and stone-pot fish argue his legend.

chinese.n: Cheng Du Chinese Restaurant 成都
chinese.s: Sichuan-family-owned West Broad spot locals rank beside Chang — dan dan noodles, tea-smoked duck and real Chengdu flavor without the crowds.
Old-school Cantonese anchor on Horsepen — weekend push-cart dim sum (11–3), roast duck 烧鸭 in the window, zero Americanization.
Shanghai street-food concept at Willow Lawn — hand-folded 小笼包, spicy wontons and wok-tossed noodles made for sharing.
All-you-can-eat Chinese hot pot 火锅 with a Korean grill at every table — the broth-and-banter format that makes group dinners easy.
Warehouse-sized pan-Asian grocery — live seafood tanks, roast duck at the deli and every hot-pot and Sichuan pantry item you'd haul back from Chengdu.
Sleek Taiwanese bakery-café in Midlothian — sea-salt cream teas, fresh-milk boba and mousse cakes; quiet-afternoon-date friendly.
The museum's free annual Lunar New Year festival (early Feb) — lion dances, calligraphy and art workshops; Richmond's biggest 春节 party, 21+ years running.

Szechuan-rooted kitchen in Mechanicsville — mala stone pots, water-boiled fish, cumin lamb, Chongqing dry-chili chicken and dan dan noodles, with hand-pleated soup dumplings to open. The north-side alternative to the Peter Chang drive.
Fan-district dumpling counter a block off VCU's campus — fillings ground fresh daily, vegetables hand-chopped, and a house peanut sauce; the cheap, quick dumpling fix in town.

fishing.s: Wade class I–II riffles for scrappy urban smallmouth minutes from downtown — VA freshwater license required (state salt- and freshwater licenses are separate).
North-bank rock gardens and eddies holding smallmouth, cats and the odd walleye — footbridge in from Texas Ave keeps crowds thin.
Ramp right at the fall line where the spring shad run stacks stripers and blue cats within a cast of the skyline — bank access too.
Calm water above the fall line for kayak smallmouth and cats — the easiest boat-fishing entry inside city limits.
Paddle the eagle-filled tidal lagoon at Henricus for blue cats, bowfin and largemouth — freshwater license covers all of Richmond's tidal James.
Main launch for the trophy tidal-James blue cat water — the stretch down to Dutch Gap gives up 50-plus-pounders all winter.

fishing.n: Tidal James Blue Cat Charter (Fish Unlimited)
fishing.s: Richmond-based guide service hunting 50–80 lb monster blues on the tidal James — tackle provided, winter is prime, licenses on you.
Bank-fish Swan and Shields for stocked channel cats and bass — Shields even gets trout stockings Nov–Mar; freshwater license applies.
Electric-only state-park lake with largemouth, crappie and summer jon-boat/kayak rentals — pair a dawn bite with the MTB trails.
Upper-James state park with canoe launches for classic smallmouth float trips — rent-a-canoe simple, camp-and-fish weekends.

biking.s: THE famous in-city loop — rocky, playful James River Park singletrack strung along both banks with river views the whole way; cross at the Nickel Bridge and Belle Isle.
Tight, rooty race lap (XTERRA and cyclocross history) dropping through ravines to Reedy Creek — sneaky-hard fun that links straight into Buttermilk.
The metro's big destination network — 30-plus miles of purpose-built MTB from Bright Hope flow to techy old-school, plus lake swims after.
100 wooded acres of twisty, sandy-fast singletrack inside city limits — the go-to ride when everything else is wet.
Hanover's 254-acre web of rooty, creek-crossed trails with a classic 6-mile race loop — unmarked, so ride with Trailforks up.
Mellow, flowy West End loops perfect for shaking off rust or a first MTB date lap — busy, friendly, easy parking.
51.7 glass-smooth paved miles from Great Shiplock Park to Williamsburg through river-plantation country — ride as far as your legs vote.
About 5 miles of RVA MORE singletrack in a wooded South Side park — mostly easy to moderate, with the harder sections toward the north end. Shared with hikers and dog walkers.
The Eastern Virginia MTB Association's 20-mile destination network in James City County — bridges, built ramps and a jump on the big downhill, with long climbs to earn it. An hour down I-64.
About 26 miles of locally maintained singletrack threading the ravines and small hills above the York River — easy to intermediate, well kept and fast enough that it hosts races.

social.s: Free lesson at 8, then Latin DJs pack the floor of the Shockoe Cuban joint — $5 cover, genuinely beginner-friendly.
RVA Dance's weekly west-end party — intro lesson 8:30, then bachata, salsa and kizomba till midnight; $7, no partner needed.
First-Tuesday salsa/bachata/merengue party at the Midlothian mega-alley — free entry, lesson first, rotating DJs.
Free Wednesday brewery run — 1/3/5-mile groups at every pace with discounted pints after; the easiest cold-open social in RVA.
Casual multi-language meetup over beers at Ardent Craft Ales — English, Spanish, Chinese 中文 and more; all levels genuinely welcome.
Monthly Broad Street gallery crawl — openings, vendors and live music from Monroe to 7th; built for wandering and easy conversation.

social.n: RVA Big Market at Bryan Park
social.s: Year-round Saturday market with dozens of Virginia makers, food trucks and coffee — the kind of line where people actually chat.
Bassist Mike Hawkins curates pickup bands all night at this Carytown listening room — $7, musicians free, the crowd listens then mingles.
$5 beginner ballroom/Latin/swing lesson at 6, then a $10-all-in social dance till 9 — explicitly singles-friendly, partners rotate.
Cap City trivia at the Manchester taproom — teams form loose, prizes for the top two, dogs welcome.
RVA Swing's monthly dance at its Lakeside Towne Center studio — beginner lesson at 7, DJ'd social dancing from 8; sliding scale $5–10 at the door.

remote.s: Suite 300 at 1806 Summit Ave in Scott's Addition. Phone and privacy booths, an unlimited coffee & tea bar and stocked café, copy/print, free parking and 24/7 member access. Meeting rooms are $69/hr, and the $199/mo Global plan opens every Venture X.
remote.p: $25 day pass · $60 day office · $99/mo community · $299/mo dedicated desk
remote.b: Peaceful, low-key floor, per a 2026 member review

remote.s: Downtown coworking at 313 E Broad St in the Arts District. High-speed Wi-Fi, privacy booths, complimentary coffee, tea and cookies, printer, outdoor space, bike storage, pet-friendly, staffed reception; M–F 8a–5p. The Convention Center deck and the 2nd & Grace garage are about a block away. Sister Gathers in Scott's Addition and Short Pump.
remote.p: Day pass from $50 · coworking from $275/mo · meeting rooms from $30/hr
remote.b: Quiet and well lit, per member reviews

remote.s: Small coworking and events space at 2309 W Main St in the Fan. Complimentary coffee & tea, high-speed internet, a kitchen, privacy booths for calls and lockers; members get 24/7 access.
remote.p: Day pass from $25 · from $165/mo · desk from $295/mo
remote.b: Small, calm space, with 16 desks upstairs

remote.s: On the Carytown strip at 3429 W Cary St. High-speed Wi-Fi, coffee & tea, a full kitchen with a pool table, printer/copier, reception, mail and fax. Meeting rooms from $35/hr come with A/V and videoconferencing. Notary and legal services are available through the community; open 24/7.
remote.p: From $15/hr · day pass from $50 · coworking from $250/mo · day office from $125

remote.s: Main Library at 101 E Franklin St, downtown. Free Wi-Fi, public computers, study rooms for 8–12 booked online, free local and long-distance faxing, 15¢ copies and notary by appointment. On-street parking, a surface lot at 1st & E Grace and a deck at 2nd & E Franklin; the spaces behind the library are permit-only. Mon–Thu 9–8, Fri 9–6, Sat 9–5, Sun 1–5.
remote.b: Really quiet, with lots of seating; weekday mornings calmest

remote.s: The state library at 800 E Broad St, downtown. Free open Wi-Fi (LVA-Guest) in all public areas, first-come reading-room computers with no time limit, free book scanners, and WHISK café (espresso, sandwiches, soups) on the first floor. Limited free validated parking in the garage under the building. Research areas Tue–Fri 9–5 plus select Saturdays; lobby Mon–Sat 8:30–5.
remote.b: Spacious, quiet reading room with ample seating

remote.s: Henrico County library at 2100 Libbie Lake East St, in the Libbie Mill development. A quiet reading room, conference and study rooms you book online, a Digital Media Lab, public computers, printing & copying and parking for about 235 cars. Mon–Thu 9–9, Fri–Sat 9–6, Sun 1–5.

Bank-run café at 2933 W Cary St in Carytown with free Wi-Fi, coffee and drinks, and a free lot across S Sheppard St. Its community rooms are free but bookable only by eligible nonprofits and student groups (2 hr/day). One reviewer's corporate VPN wouldn't connect on the café network, so test before you count on it.
remote.b: Plenty of seats, with outlets upstairs; parking tight at peak

remote.s: Blanchard's first café, at 3121 W Broad St across from Scott's Addition — a big open room that RICtoday's remote-work guide lists for free Wi-Fi and ample seating. The roaster (in Richmond since 2005) runs free slow bars, brew classes and cuppings in its café classroom Mon, Wed & Fri. Mon–Fri 7a–5p, Sat–Sun 8a–5p.
remote.b: Often at full capacity, busiest Sunday at noon; quiet room inside

remote.s: North Side coffeehouse at 4015 MacArthur Ave, serving the neighborhood since 2002 and on RICtoday's short list of Richmond cafés with free Wi-Fi, ample seating and a good working atmosphere. Breakfast wraps, sandwiches, salads and fresh baked goods; open every day until 3p.
remote.b: Very busy on weekends; weekdays easier

events.s: The holiday rom-com on the big screen with its score played live, at the Carpenter Theatre in Dominion Energy Center. An easy date night.

Lewis Ginter Botanical Garden's huge holiday light show. Look for 18+ 'GardenFest for Grownups' nights (12/2, 12/3, 12/30) and live-performance nights. Buy timed tickets ahead, since walk-ups are limited.
The leg-lamp and Red Ryder BB gun musical over Thanksgiving weekend at the Altria Theater.
The Richmond Symphony's annual Messiah at the Carpenter Theatre, opening the holiday season.
The Dancing with the Stars champ's touring dance show at the Altria Theater.
Richmond's beloved Nutcracker, choreographed by Stoner Winslett, with the Richmond Symphony playing live at the Carpenter Theatre.
A brand-new holiday circus at the Altria, with acrobats and aerialists set to seasonal music; doors at 6:30p.
Tig Notaro's deadpan stand-up at the Carpenter Theatre.
An MLK-weekend hip-hop and R&B bill at the Altria: Kevin Gates headlines, with R&B singer VEDO and Houston rapper KenTheMan.
The ventriloquist and his cast of puppets at the Altria Theater.
The crosstown Capital City Classic: the Rams host the Spiders at a packed Siegel Center, with the Peppas pep band.
Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop musical about the founding fathers, back at the Altria for a two-week run.
The Rams play their first home game of the season at the Siegel Center on Broad St, a short ride up Broad St from downtown.
Leoncavallo's opera about a jealous clown is staged at the Carpenter Theatre in the Dominion Energy Center, with a Friday evening show and a Sunday matinee.
The Richmond Symphony plays the score live while the 1985 adventure film screens at the Altria Theater. Showtime moved to 6p.
The cult 1986 fantasy film screens with its score performed live at the Carpenter Theatre in the Dominion Energy Center.
Richmond's big holiday parade of floats, bands and giant balloons comes down Broad St. The 2026 route is reversed and finishes at the Science Museum.
More than 75 artisans sell handmade gifts on the Carriage House Lawn at Maymont, with fire pits, carolers, a mulled-wine bar and holiday tours of the mansion, noon to 5p.
Cadence Theatre, ATLAS Partnership and THE HOUSE stage the musical at the Gottwald Playhouse in the Dominion Energy Center, with evening and matinee shows.
The tenth annual Richmond hip-hop showcase at The Broadberry, with Nickelus F, Radio B and Michael Millions headlining and an RVA rap cypher opening. Doors at 6p.

iceskating.s: Year-round ice in Short Pump, with laser tag and an arcade under the same roof on Pouncey Tract Rd (44,000 sq ft of ice and games). Public sessions run almost every day: $16 admission and $4 figure or hockey rentals, subject to availability, and kids 4 and under skate free with an adult. Times post weekly on the Richmond Skating site.

The Chesterfield-side sister rink to SkateNation, just off Midlothian Turnpike near Johnston-Willis Hospital, open all year. It runs public skating most days plus Learn to Skate, figure skating and hockey programs. Pricing matches Short Pump ($16 in, $4 rentals, under-5s free with an adult); check the Midlothian schedule page before driving.

The ballpark becomes a holiday festival Nov 19, 2026–Jan 3, 2027, with an outdoor ice rink at its heart. Skating is a timed add-on to festival admission. Hours are Wed–Thu 5–10p, Fri–Sat 4–11p and Sun 4–10p, with longer hours over the holidays and select Mon/Tue closures before Dec 18. Parking costs $8 in advance or $10 on the day.

The mall's seasonal outdoor rink returns Nov 14, 2026–Jan 11, 2027. General admission with skate rental is $16; groups of 15 or more pay $12–13, and skate aids rent for $8. Weekday sessions mostly run 3–7p, weekends from late morning, and it's closed Thanksgiving. A tree lighting on Nov 21 and holiday events run rinkside through December.

Chesterfield's newest ice opened July 2026 near River City Sportsplex in Brandermill: a 49,000 sq ft venue with an NHL-size sheet, 350 seats and six locker rooms. It is built around youth and adult hockey and figure skating, and also offers public skating with rental skates. A second sheet is planned. Check session times before driving out.

Colonial Williamsburg's open-air rink on Duke of Gloucester St, a day trip down I-64 from Richmond. It's open daily Nov 20, 2026–Feb 28, 2027, holidays included. A day of skating costs $18 for ages 13+ and $13 for ages 3–12; rentals are $7 and season passes $125/$95. Payment is card-only. Merchants Square across the street has dinner.

skating.n: Virginia Capital Trail from Great Shiplock Park
skating.s: The paved, car-free trail starts at Great Shiplock Park by the downtown floodgates and runs 51.7 miles east to Jamestown, 8–10 ft wide. Trail rules cover all wheels: yield to walkers, keep right, call your passes. The Richmond end is rolling; the flatter miles are toward Jamestown, and about 30 wooden bridges interrupt the asphalt.

Henrico's big roller rink on Williamsburg Rd east of downtown, with an arcade, laser tag, pool tables and a food court under one roof, and a home base for roller derby teams. Wednesday sessions are adults only (18+), adult nights with DJs run twice a month, and coaches teach on Saturdays. Kids under 10 get two free passes through Kids Skate Free.

A monthly all-ages, alcohol-free skate night at Roller Dome, with drag performances and a rink full of the local skate community. The July 2026 edition ran 6–9p for $10. It's the most welcoming way into Richmond's roller crowd; check The Phil's calendar for the next date.

A classic family rink on N. Washington Hwy in Ashland with a posted weekly schedule: three public sessions on Saturdays, Sun 2–4:30p, Fri 8–10:30p and a Thursday-morning skate, plus an 18+ adult skate Mondays 7:30–10p. Admission runs $7–10, rentals are $5 and skate mates for beginners $5. Roller hockey and classes too.

skating.n: Fall Line Trail (Ashland to Woodman Rd)
skating.s: The first regional piece of the planned 43-mile Ashland-to-Petersburg trail: a 4.8-mile paved section, opened Sept 2025, running from Ashland's Trolley Line Trail through Hanover to Woodman Rd in Henrico. Start at the Carter Park trailhead, with parking just across the street. The links south into Richmond are still being designed and built.

Henrico's 10-ft-wide asphalt connector, extended to nearly three-quarters of a mile, links Dorey Park in Varina to the Virginia Capital Trail. The park's lot makes an easy start for skating the Cap Trail east without beginning in downtown traffic. Expect bikes and runners merging on and off the main trail.

skating.n: Virginia Capital Trail – Charles City Courthouse section
skating.s: The Cap Trail's quiet middle. An inline skater on TrailLink rated the ~6-mile section near Charles City Courthouse smooth and generally flat, with a couple of turns, small hills and few intersections; park at the courthouse and roll a block to the trail. The review dates from 2011, but TrailLink still lists the whole 52 miles for inline skating.
